findings.title: Cancellation-side degradation is undefined for reachable no-active-generation tuples
findings.requirement_or_contract: The IXH cancellation-side degradation relation must be total over every reachable nonterminal HEALTHY REQUESTED|QUIESCING|CLEANING tuple and must define a constructible deterministic receipt for every member, including tuples with no active canary generation.
evidence: docs/state-transition-manifests.md:1042 makes a HEALTHY, no-active-generation tuple an explicit ordinary IH01 source before cancellation.
docs/state-transition-manifests.md:1004 rejects ordinary IH01 while cancellation is not NONE, and :1008 permits IX01 from every reachable nonterminal tuple.
docs/state-transition-manifests.md:1023 requires a current-generation degradation and a generation-bound receipt for IXH01-R.
docs/state-transition-manifests.md:1029 claims all reachable nonterminal HEALTHY cancellation tuples are covered but hashes active_canary_generation without defining a no-generation/null encoding.
PLAN.md:238 materially claims that control degradation always commits after cancellation and that the generated relation equals all such reachable tuples.
findings.impact: A valid IX01-before-degradation interleaving from an inactive/no-exposure tuple must drop the degradation or invent an undefined receipt identity. The exact-equality and always-record claims are therefore not implementable from the current contract.
findings.required_correction: Add an explicit cancellation-side no-active-generation guard/receipt partition, or define a canonical nullable generation identity used by IXH01-R/Q/C and CancellationDegradationReceipt. Then require generated source equality for active-generation and no-generation sources and add IX01-before-IH01 race witnesses for inactive/no-exposure tuples.
